faults.quote: I don't have cost per seat mile trend.
faults.why: The ledger's unit_costs and fuel_prices items say costs per flight and fuel prices were flat, which coarsely answers the cost-trend ask. The answer only reached the candidate indirectly, through exhibit-1 at t8 and exhibit-2 at t14.

faults.quote: Is that MECE, and what's missing? Specifically, what within revenue could you still be missing before you commit to pricing?
faults.why: Three questions are stacked into one turn.

faults.quote: I'm afraid I don't have quarter-by-quarter fares and passengers since entry.
faults.why: The candidate also asked how many seats a day the entrant had added. That ask got no release, refusal or deferral.

faults.quote: As the exhibit shows: Variable cost on the new routes is estimated at $9,200 per flight, across 5,000 flights a year that would use the aircraft time freed by exiting Hub–Lakeport (2,000 flights) and Hub–Port Avery (3,000 flights).
faults.why: The candidate asked for launch costs (marketing, station setup, crew basing). The interviewer repeated an exhibit line that doesn't answer this and never said it doesn't have launch costs.

faults.quote: Before we wrap up — you said each passenger nets $160 toward the $9,200 variable cost.
faults.why: The candidate stated a want for O&D volume on each new city pair. It got no word, not even an 'I don't have that', before the case closed.
